newsitem.title: USA: Eclipse sees short-term lower U.S. revs.
newsitem.headline: Eclipse sees short-term lower U.S. revs.

text.p: Eclipse Surgical Technologies Inc said Tuesday a new medicare reimbursement ruling will result in a significant increase in clinical trial expenses and a significant reduction in U.S. revenues, at least over the short term.

The company said in a statement that the ruling, by the Healthcare Finance Administration (HCFA) on the transmyocardial revascularization (TMR) industry, institutes a non-coverage policy for all TMR procedures performed on Medicare patients in the United States, effective May 19.
TMR is an investigational procedure that may be performed on a beating heart using a special holmium laser device to create pathways within the heart muscle.

"While we are disappointed with the HCFA ruling, we are hopeful that once the U.S. Food and Drug Administration grants marketing clearance for TMR to any TMR company, HCFA will reconsider coverage of the procedure," said Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Dr. Douglas Murphy-Chutorian.
The company said it has completed Phase II clinical trials comparing TMR to drug therapy and expects to file for pre-marketing approval with the FDA by mid-summer.
